papers.title: Label-free multi-metric pipeline for reproducible clustering of single-cell RNA-seq cell types.
papers.abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing has transformed our ability to identify cell types and explore cellular diversity. However, determining whether apparent cell subtypes represent true biological populations or artifacts of data analysis remains a major challenge. To address this issue, we developed scClustBench, an open-source benchmarking framework that evaluates cluster quality, stability, and reproducibility across multiple analytical approaches. Rather than relying on a single clustering method, scClustBench tests whether proposed cell subtypes can be consistently recovered. We applied scClustBen
papers.summary: The authors present scClustBench, an open-source benchmarking framework that evaluates single-cell RNA-seq clustering by testing cluster quality, stability, and reproducibility across multiple analytical approaches rather than relying on a single method. The tool helps distinguish true biological cell subtypes from analysis artifacts by checking whether proposed clusters can be consistently recovered.

papers.title: Integrative multi-omic mapping of urinary and intrarenal immune landscapes in lupus nephritis identifies convergent inflammatory and fibrotic programs.
papers.abstract: Renal biopsy is the gold standard for classifying lupus nephritis (LN), but due to its invasiveness and difficult longitudinal follow-up, it incompletely captures immune and histopathological dynamics. Urinary single-cell transcriptomic analysis has been proposed as a minimally invasive approach for monitoring LN, while renal single-cell and spatial transcriptomics provide high-resolution reference maps of the intrarenal environment. We performed a systematic scoping review following PRISMA-ScR guidelines to evaluate direct urinary-renal transcriptomic concordance and pathway molecular converg
papers.summary: This scoping review examines how well minimally invasive urinary single-cell transcriptomics reflects the intrarenal immune landscape in lupus nephritis, comparing it against renal single-cell and spatial transcriptomic reference maps. The authors identify convergent inflammatory and fibrotic programs across urinary and kidney compartments, supporting urine-based monitoring as a surrogate for biopsy. The work maps the current evidence base and highlights where direct urinary-renal concordance remains to be established.

papers.title: CD44+ Proximal Tubular Epithelial Cells May Be Involved in Renal Fibrosis and Inflammation via TGF-β Signaling in Hyperuricemic Nephropathy.
papers.abstract: The prevalence of hyperuricemia (HUA) is continuously increasing and HUA may eventually develop into irreversible hyperuricemic nephropathy (HN). Injured proximal tubule (PT) in the HUA microenvironment plays an important role in the progression of HN. However, the underlying pathological mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) between HUA kidneys and control groups were screened from bulk RNA sequencing data to identify abnormally activated signaling. Subsequently, PT cell-subtypes related to injury and repair were identified in single-cell RNA sequenc
papers.journal: Journal of cell communication and signaling
papers.summary: This study combines bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing to identify CD44+ proximal tubular epithelial cells as a key subpopulation in hyperuricemic nephropathy. These cells appear to drive renal fibrosis and inflammation through TGF-β signaling, suggesting a potential therapeutic target for preventing kidney damage in hyperuricemia.

papers.title: Generating scRNA-seq data from bulk RNA-seq using a Gaussian mixture variational autoencoder.
papers.abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) provides detailed, genome-wide gene expression profiles at single-cell resolution, enabling the identification of disease-driving cell types and genes. However, scRNA-seq remains costly, and there are extremely limited samples generated in even the most extensive human disease studies. In contrast, bulk RNA-seq data is abundant but averages gene expression across all cell types, losing cell-specific detail. To further leverage this abundance of RNA-seq data, methods have been developed to infer cell type proportions and average expression from bulk data u
papers.summary: The authors present a Gaussian mixture variational autoencoder that reconstructs single-cell RNA-seq expression profiles from bulk RNA-seq data, aiming to recover cell-type-specific detail lost in bulk averaging. This lets existing large bulk datasets be mined for single-cell-level insights without new scRNA-seq experiments. The work is a computational deconvolution/generation method rather than a biological discovery.

papers.title: Ultralow-volume shallow microwell-based collection and processing for scalable spatial proteome mapping of tissues.
papers.abstract: Multi-ome mapping technologies for precise comprehensive characterization of tissues at high spatial resolutions are crucial for providing insights into tissue heterogeneity and microenvironment within spatial context. However, proteome mapping technologies lag far behind other transcriptome (genome) mapping technologies. Here we report an Ultralow-volume, Shallow, Microwell plate-based voxel Collection and Processing coupled with mass spectrometry (MS) method, termed USMCP-MS, for robust scalable proteome mapping of tissues at high spatial resolutions. This method was built upon the design of
papers.summary: The authors present USMCP-MS, a method that uses ultralow-volume shallow microwell plates to collect and process tissue voxels for mass-spectrometry-based spatial proteome mapping. This addresses the lag of spatial proteomics behind spatial transcriptomics by enabling robust, scalable proteome mapping at high spatial resolution.

papers.title: GLAND: Resolving small and non-continuous tissue domains via a hybrid attention mechanism.
papers.abstract: Recent advances in spatial transcriptomic technology provide unprecedented insights into tissue architecture by enabling high-throughput gene expression profiling with the corresponding spatial context. While identifying spatial domains is a prerequisite for understanding tissue heterogeneity and functional organization, current computational methods often fail to resolve non-continuous or small domains that, despite their biological significance, exhibit complex spatial distribution.
papers.summary: GLAND is a new computational method for identifying spatial domains in spatial transcriptomics data, using a hybrid attention mechanism to better resolve small or non-continuous tissue domains that existing methods struggle with. This addresses a key gap in spatial domain detection, where biologically important structures with complex spatial distributions are often missed.

papers.title: Spatially Resolved Transcriptomic Correlation Improves the Prediction of Anticancer Drug Candidates.
papers.abstract: Predicting the anticancer effects of compounds is critical for computational drug evaluation. However, traditional transcriptomics-based virtual screening relies on bulk RNA profiling, causing intratumoral spatial heterogeneity to be averaged across the entire tissue and thereby limiting predictive accuracy. This limitation is particularly consequential for triple-negative breast cancer, which lacks receptor-guided treatment options and exhibits pronounced spatial heterogeneity that can obscure region-specific therapeutic vulnerabilities when assessed by bulk analysis alone. To address this li
papers.journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling
papers.summary: The authors propose using spatially resolved transcriptomics rather than bulk RNA profiling to predict anticancer drug candidates, arguing that bulk analysis averages out intratumoral spatial heterogeneity. They apply this to triple-negative breast cancer, where spatial heterogeneity can obscure region-specific therapeutic vulnerabilities. The approach aims to improve virtual screening accuracy by incorporating spatial correlation of gene expression.

papers.title: Integrated transcriptomics reveal fibroblast-monocyte crosstalk with JAK-STAT activation associated with Parvimonas micra-induced periodontitis.
papers.abstract: This study aimed to characterize the spatial and molecular mechanisms of Parvimonas micra-induced periodontitis, which remains poorly understood. We used bulk RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomics to investigate gingival responses in ligature and P. micra-induced rat periodontitis model and validated the findings in human patients. In rat periodontitis model, significant transcriptomic changes occurred across gingival regions, especially in the suprabasal epithelium, affecting autophagy and immune defense. Both bulk and spatial transcriptomic analyses indicate that JAK-STAT signaling was
papers.summary: Using bulk and spatial transcriptomics in a rat periodontitis model, the authors show that Parvimonas micra infection drives region-specific gingival transcriptomic changes, particularly in suprabasal epithelium affecting autophagy and immune defense. Integrated analyses reveal fibroblast-monocyte crosstalk with JAK-STAT pathway activation, which was validated in human periodontitis patients. The work implicates a specific microbial species and a druggable signaling axis in disease pathogenesis.

papers.title: Integrative Genetic and Transcriptomic Analysis Reveals Macrophage-Associated Signatures and Predicted Macrophage-Fibroblast Communication in Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension.
papers.abstract: How macrophage-associated expression changes relate to fibroblast extracellular matrix (ECM) programs in pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) remains incompletely understood. This study aimed to characterize the relationship between clinically associated macrophage expression patterns and fibroblast ECM programs and to examine their spatial correspondence.
papers.summary: This study integrates genetic and transcriptomic data to identify macrophage-associated gene expression signatures linked to pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) and predicts communication between macrophages and fibroblasts that may drive extracellular matrix remodeling. The authors characterize how these macrophage expression patterns correspond spatially to fibroblast ECM programs, suggesting a role for immune-stromal crosstalk in PAH pathogenesis.

papers.title: AI-driven multi-omics identifies SPP1⁺ tumor-associated macrophages as a therapeutic target and predicts lymph node metastasis in papillary thyroid cancer.
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming drug design by enabling the systematic discovery of therapeutic targets and the prediction of drug response from complex biomedical data. In papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC), lymph node metastasis remains a key determinant of poor outcome, yet targetable drivers and predictive models for metastasis are lacking. Here, we integrate single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, and machine learning to identify SPP1⁺ tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) as a functionally validated driver of lymph node metastasis in PTC. Using single-cell and spat
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, and machine learning to identify SPP1⁺ tumor-associated macrophages as a driver of lymph node metastasis in papillary thyroid cancer. The authors functionally validate this macrophage population as a therapeutic target and develop a predictive model for metastasis. The work demonstrates how AI-driven multi-omics can uncover targetable cell populations and support clinical prediction in PTC.

papers.title: Identification of immune pathways regulating the cell mediated immunity in leishmaniasis in humans.
papers.abstract: A delayed-type hypersensitivity (DTH) response induced by the intradermal inoculation of leishmanin antigen induced in individuals exposed to parasite Leishmania is a reliable indicator of cell mediated immunity (CMI). Leishmanin antigen skin test (LST) is also an important tool in disease surveillance studies in endemic area and can be used to assess vaccine efficacy. Previous studies assessing CMI in Leishmania exposed individuals were limited to analysis of PBMCs. To investigate the mediators of CMI, we performed spatial transcriptomic analysis of the DTH skin biopsies after leishmanin anti
papers.summary: This study used spatial transcriptomics on skin biopsies from leishmanin skin tests to map the immune pathways underlying cell-mediated immunity to Leishmania in humans. It moves beyond prior PBMC-based analyses by profiling the local tissue response in situ, identifying immune mediators and pathways associated with delayed-type hypersensitivity. The work provides a tissue-level resource for understanding protective immunity and for evaluating vaccine efficacy in leishmaniasis.

papers.title: Beyond Genomic Alterations: Transcriptomic Profiling of Lineage Plasticity in Metastatic Solid Tumors.
papers.abstract: Lineage plasticity allows tumor cells to shift their differentiation state during metastatic progression and treatment. Genomic profiling identifies driver alterations and clonal relationships but does not fully characterize the lineage programs expressed by metastatic lesions. This review examines the complementary role of transcriptomic profiling and histopathology in assessing changes in tumor identity, with emphasis on colorectal, pancreatic, prostate, and lung cancers. We discuss studies of lineage transformation, intermediate cellular states, and loss of lineage fidelity, and their relat
papers.summary: This review argues that genomic profiling alone cannot capture the lineage plasticity that drives metastatic progression and treatment resistance in solid tumors. It surveys transcriptomic and histopathological evidence of lineage transformation, intermediate cellular states, and loss of lineage fidelity in colorectal, pancreatic, prostate, and lung cancers, positioning transcriptomic profiling as a necessary complement to DNA-based diagnostics.

papers.title: Iterative Geometric Structure Guided Nonnegative Matrix Factorization Scheme for Bulk Tissue RNA-seq Data Deconvolution.
papers.abstract: Complete deconvolution is a class of unsupervised methods that aim to estimate both cell-type proportions and cell-type-specific gene expression profiles (GEPs) from bulk RNA-seq data, without requiring prior reference profiles. Hence, it enables broader applicability to tissues or species for which reference data are limited or unavailable. For many existing methods, nonnegative matrix factorization (NMF) serves as the fundamental computational tool. However, NMF is mathematically ill-posed and a comprehensive understanding of how to overcome the inherent ill-posedness and improve solution ac
papers.summary: This paper introduces an iterative geometric structure-guided nonnegative matrix factorization (NMF) method for complete deconvolution of bulk RNA-seq data, estimating both cell-type proportions and cell-type-specific gene expression profiles without reference profiles. The approach addresses the mathematical ill-posedness of standard NMF by incorporating geometric structure to constrain and improve solutions. This enables deconvolution in tissues or species lacking reference data.

papers.title: Imaging Tumor Plasticity Across Space and Time: From Cell State to Metastatic Dissemination.
papers.abstract: Cancer cell plasticity-the capacity of tumor cells to alter phenotypic and functional states under microenvironmental and therapeutic pressure-contributes to invasion, metastasis, and therapy resistance, but is poorly captured by endpoint assays. This review asks which manifestations of plasticity current imaging and spatially resolved technologies can detect, and which conclusions their signals support. We critically reviewed studies using fluorescent and bioluminescent reporters, intravital microscopy, tissue clearing and light-sheet microscopy, spatial transcriptomics, multiplexed imaging,
papers.summary: This review examines how current imaging and spatially resolved technologies can detect cancer cell plasticity—the ability of tumor cells to change phenotype under microenvironmental and therapeutic pressure—and what conclusions these signals actually support. It critically surveys fluorescent/bioluminescent reporters, intravital microscopy, tissue clearing and light-sheet microscopy, spatial transcriptomics, and multiplexed imaging, arguing that endpoint assays poorly capture plasticity and that each modality has distinct interpretive limits. The work is a conceptual and methodological synthesis rather than a new dataset.

papers.title: Integrated multi-omics and experimental analyses characterize an IGF2BP3-MMP7-associated pattern in extracellular matrix remodeling and Treg-associated immune suppression in pancreatic adenocarcinoma.
papers.abstract: Pancreatic adenocarcinoma (PAAD) is characterized by extensive extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling and a profoundly immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. As an important N6-methyladenosine (m6A) reader, insulin-like growth factor 2 mRNA-binding protein 3 (IGF2BP3) has been implicated in tumor progression; however, its downstream regulatory network and potential role in immune microenvironment remodeling remain incompletely understood.
papers.summary: This study integrates multi-omics data with experimental validation to characterize how the m6A reader IGF2BP3, together with MMP7, contributes to extracellular matrix remodeling and Treg-mediated immune suppression in pancreatic adenocarcinoma. The work links an RNA-binding protein to ECM and immunosuppressive programs, suggesting a potential regulatory axis in PAAD progression.

papers.title: REV-ERBα/β Disruption Drives Environmental Tobacco Smoke-Induced Cellular Senescence Associated with cGAS-STING Signaling Promoting Lung Remodeling.
papers.abstract: Cellular senescence and DNA damage are recognized contributors to smoke-induced lung injury. However, how these processes integrate with circadian regulation and innate immune sensing in response to environmental stressors remains incompletely understood. Here, we identify a conserved multi-lineage transcriptional program in murine lungs that we define as the SCPS axis, characterized by Suppressed Clock, Primed Senescence (SCPS), fibrinolytic Shutdown, and cGAS-STING activation. We show that environmental cigarette/tobacco smoke (ETS) exposure induces senescence and SASP factor production in b
papers.summary: This study identifies a conserved transcriptional program in mouse lungs, termed the SCPS axis, that links circadian clock suppression (via REV-ERBα/β disruption) to cellular senescence, fibrinolytic shutdown, and cGAS-STING innate immune activation after environmental tobacco smoke exposure. The authors show that ETS-induced senescence and SASP production are driven by disruption of REV-ERBα/β and are associated with cGAS-STING signaling, contributing to lung remodeling. The work connects circadian regulation, senescence, and innate immune sensing in smoke-induced lung injury.

papers.title: ADAMTS9-AS1 and ADRA1D Are associated with urea cycle activity and ammonia stress responses in prostate cancer.
papers.abstract: Prostate cancer (PRAD) progression is closely associated with metabolic reprogramming, but the role of nitrogen metabolism and ammonia-associated cell death remains unclear. This study investigates the clinical and functional significance of urea cycle activity in PRAD.
papers.summary: This study examines how urea cycle activity and ammonia-related stress responses contribute to prostate cancer progression, identifying ADAMTS9-AS1 and ADRA1D as genes associated with these processes. The findings suggest that nitrogen metabolism and ammonia-induced cell death pathways may have clinical and functional relevance in prostate cancer.

papers.title: A versatile set of computational tools for inference of genetic ancestry from human molecular data.
papers.abstract: Molecular properties of human diseases and conditions often exhibit dependence on the genetic ancestry of the donor. In order to make more human molecular data available for ancestry-informed research, we developed a set of software tools termed Robust Ancestry Inference using Data Synthesis (RAIDS) for inference of genetic ancestry from sequence data that pose challenges to genotyping. The data-synthesis procedure, underlying RAIDS, makes it a unique tool capable of assessing and optimizing the accuracy of inference for each individual molecular profile, with no resort to cohort data. Here we
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors present RAIDS, a software toolkit that infers genetic ancestry directly from human molecular data, including sequence data that are difficult to genotype. Its data-synthesis approach lets it assess and optimize ancestry-inference accuracy for each individual sample without needing cohort data.

papers.title: FViT: A Foundation-Tokenized Vision Transformer with Retrieval-Augmented Multi-Scale Ensembling for Deep Learning-Based Spatial Gene Expression Prediction from Histopathology.
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics links gene expression to tissue morphology but is too costly for routine clinical use, motivating prediction of expression from hematoxylin-and-eosin (H&E) images. FViT (Foundation-tokenized Vision Transformer) tokenizes a spot and its k nearest neighbours with the frozen foundation model Phikon, fuses the tokens with a small trainable Transformer with a relative-position embedding, predicts expression directly and by k-nearest-neighbour retrieval of measured training expression, and combines three neighbourhood sizes (k = 8, 16, 24) in a weighted ensemble. We evaluated
papers.summary: FViT predicts spatial gene expression from routine H&E histology images by tokenizing each tissue spot and its nearest neighbors with a frozen foundation model (Phikon), fusing these tokens with a small trainable Transformer, and combining direct prediction with k-nearest-neighbor retrieval of measured training expression across three neighborhood sizes. This retrieval-augmented, multi-scale ensembling approach aims to make spatial transcriptomics more accessible by inferring expression profiles from cheap histology slides rather than costly assays.

papers.title: SigBridgeR: An R Toolkit for Standardized Identification and Benchmarking of Phenotype-Associated Cell Subpopulations in Single-Cell Transcriptomics.
papers.abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) has revolutionized our understanding of cellular heterogeneity, yet linking specific cell subpopulations to clinically relevant phenotypes remains a major challenge. Although multiple computational methods have been developed to integrate bulk transcriptomic and single-cell data for phenotype-associated cell identification, differences in algorithmic strategies, parameter configurations, software implementations, and output formats make it difficult to compare methods fairly, reproduce analyses, and determine which approach is most suitable for a given bi
papers.summary: SigBridgeR is an R toolkit that standardizes the identification of phenotype-associated cell subpopulations by integrating bulk transcriptomic and single-cell RNA-seq data. It provides a unified framework for running, comparing, and benchmarking multiple computational methods, addressing inconsistencies in algorithms, parameters, and output formats that currently hinder fair comparison and reproducibility.

papers.title: Single-Cell and Spatial Transcriptomic Dissection of Macrophage-Associated Inflammatory Signalling in Endometriosis-Associated Pain: A Hypothesis-Generating Study of Candidate Tissue-Level Genes.
papers.abstract: Background: Endometriosis is an oestrogen-dependent chronic inflammatory disease with chronic pelvic pain as a predominant and disabling symptom that severely compromises patient quality of life. The molecular mechanisms governing endometriosis-associated pain remain poorly elucidated. Given the lack of individual clinical pain scores in public datasets, this hypothesis-generating study aimed to characterise pain-correlated cell subsets and signalling programmes at single-cell resolution using a literature-based inflammatory gene module, and to identify replicable tissue-level candidate genes
papers.summary: This hypothesis-generating study uses single-cell and spatial transcriptomics to characterize macrophage-associated inflammatory signaling in endometriosis-associated pain, leveraging a literature-based inflammatory gene module as a proxy for pain since individual pain scores were unavailable in public datasets. The authors identify candidate tissue-level genes and pain-correlated cell subsets, though the work is explicitly framed as exploratory and requires validation in datasets with clinical pain annotations.

papers.title: A multi-scale cell-type resolved map of trans-regulatory architecture in the aging human brain.
papers.abstract: Mapping genetic effects on distal genes and regulatory programs is essential for understanding how genetic variation influences complex diseases; yet trans-QTL discovery remains limited by weak effect sizes, extensive multiple testing and poor reproducibility. Here, we introduce TransMap, a generalizable computational framework that combines multi-scale trans-QTL mapping with multi-phenotype genetic colocalization to improve the discovery and interpretation of distal regulatory variants. Beyond individual trans-eGenes, TransMap constructs local co-regulatory program phenotypes that account for
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: The authors present TransMap, a computational framework that combines multi-scale trans-QTL mapping with multi-phenotype genetic colocalization to improve discovery and interpretation of distal regulatory variants. Applied to the aging human brain, it produces a cell-type-resolved map of trans-regulatory architecture, including local co-regulatory program phenotypes that go beyond individual trans-eGenes.

papers.title: Deciphering Hepatic Host Transcriptomic Responses to Leishmania Infection: Integrating Evidence from In Vivo and In Vitro Studies.
papers.abstract: Visceral leishmaniasis (VL) is a life-threatening, vector-borne systemic disease caused by the parasitic protozoans Leishmania donovani and Leishmania infantum. Among the affected organs, the liver represents a unique immunological environment in which, in commonly used experimental murine models, infection is often controlled through the coordinated formation of granulomas around infected Kupffer cells. However, effective hepatic parasite control does not necessarily result in complete parasite elimination, and the course of infection may vary across host species and experimental models. Unde
papers.summary: This study integrates in vivo and in vitro transcriptomic data to characterize how the liver responds to Leishmania infection, focusing on the coordinated immune and granuloma-forming processes that control but do not fully eliminate parasites. It highlights conserved hepatic host responses across experimental models while noting variation across host species and systems.

papers.title: SPACE-Tag Enables High-Throughput Spatial Chromatin Profiling With CUT&Tag.
papers.abstract: Spatial epigenomics maps chromatin states within intact tissues, yet current methods remain limited by accessibility and scale. We developed SPACE-Tag, a spatial CUT&Tag framework that converts epigenetic marks-associated DNA into polyadenylated RNA through T7-based linear amplification, enabling direct integration with standard spatial transcriptomic workflows. Applied to the mouse brain, SPACE-Tag resolved activating and repressive chromatin landscapes, recovered region-specific gene-regulatory programs across anatomical domains, and showed strong correlation with existing bulk and single-ce
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: SPACE-Tag is a new spatial CUT&Tag method that converts chromatin-associated DNA into polyadenylated RNA via T7 linear amplification, allowing spatial epigenomic profiling to be run on standard spatial transcriptomics platforms. Applied to mouse brain, it mapped activating and repressive chromatin marks, recovered region-specific regulatory programs, and correlated well with bulk and single-cell data. This lowers barriers to high-throughput spatial chromatin profiling.

papers.title: Inferring gene regulatory networks from single-cell perturbation data by optimizing causal reach of latent mediator dynamics.
papers.abstract: Resolving the causal structure of gene regulatory networks is central to understanding cellular regulation. Pooled CRISPR screens with single-cell RNA readouts measure the transcriptional consequences of many interventions in parallel, providing a powerful resource for causal discovery. Combinatorial designs that perturb multiple regulators per cell increase throughput and can reveal responses that single-gene perturbations do not. However, inferring causal gene networks from these experiments remains challenging because gene regulatory interactions are nonlinear, dynamic, and often involve fe
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors present a computational method for inferring causal gene regulatory networks from pooled CRISPR single-cell perturbation screens, including combinatorial perturbations that target multiple regulators per cell. The approach models latent mediator dynamics and optimizes the causal reach of these mediators to capture nonlinear, dynamic regulatory interactions. This addresses a key bottleneck in using high-throughput perturbation data for causal network discovery.

papers.title: Mapping the regulatory wiring of endothelial cell differentiation reveals a critical role for Hippo mechanosignaling.
papers.abstract: At each step of development, stem cells encounter a branching decision to differentiate into one type of cell or another. This decision is executed through the action of competing gene programs that specify different cellular identities. Consequently, creating a comprehensive map of the gene programs that drive each branching step of human cell differentiation remains a long-sought goal of developmental and stem cell biology. Here, we introduce a framework combining genome-wide CRISPR screens, single-cell readouts, and gene program inference to systematically discover and characterize regulato
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors developed a framework combining genome-wide CRISPR screens, single-cell readouts, and gene program inference to systematically map the regulatory programs controlling human endothelial cell differentiation. Using this approach, they identified Hippo mechanosignaling as a critical regulator of the differentiation process. The work provides a generalizable strategy for discovering gene programs that drive branching decisions during stem cell differentiation.

papers.title: gcat, its_a_scam: modular tools for single cell data processing and per-cell quality control.
papers.abstract: The era of designing bioinformatic pipelines using open source tools is giving way to monolithic, and often proprietary, tools designed for end-to-end analysis, especially in the context of single cell data. While these tools are convenient for going from sequencing data to an almost complete data analysis "in a few clicks", they can strongly limit data use beyond standard analyses.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors present gcat and its_a_scam, two modular open-source tools for single-cell data processing and per-cell quality control. They argue that monolithic end-to-end pipelines limit flexibility and data reuse, and offer these tools as composable alternatives for building custom single-cell workflows.

papers.title: Comparative molecular analysis of histopathologic subtypes reveals shared epithelial remodeling yet distinct fibroblast programs in scleroderma lung disease.
papers.abstract: Interstitial lung disease (ILD) drives mortality in systemic sclerosis (SSc), with a subset developing progressive pulmonary fibrosis (PPF) resembling idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF). Despite recognition of two distinct histopathologic patterns, the cellular basis of nonspecific interstitial pneumonia (NSIP) and usual interstitial pneumonia (UIP) remains poorly understood.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This study compares the cellular and molecular features of two lung disease patterns (NSIP and UIP) seen in scleroderma patients. It finds that both patterns share similar epithelial cell remodeling, but differ in their fibroblast programs, suggesting that the fibroblast compartment drives the distinct histopathology. This helps explain why some scleroderma patients develop progressive fibrosis resembling IPF.

papers.title: VIGAT: VLM-guided gene activity quantification from single-cell ATAC-seq.
papers.abstract: Gene activity quantification from single-cell ATAC-seq is challenging because genomic regions informative of cell identity can vary across genes and tissues, while broadly accessible regions may provide limited cell-type-discriminative information. We developed VIGAT, a vision-language model (VLM)-guided tool that automates visual interpretation of ATAC coverage plots for adaptive gene activity quantification. VIGAT jointly examines accessibility patterns across multiple marker genes, integrating genomic annotations and biological context to select gene-specific regions enriched for cluster-di
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: VIGAT is a new tool that uses a vision-language model to automatically interpret ATAC-seq coverage plots and adaptively quantify gene activity from single-cell ATAC-seq data. By jointly examining accessibility patterns across multiple marker genes and incorporating genomic annotations, it selects gene-specific regions that better discriminate cell types. This addresses the challenge that informative regulatory regions vary across genes and tissues, improving gene activity estimates for cell identity.

papers.title: DiffKnock: diffusion-based knockoff inference for neural networks with applications to single-cell RNA-sequencing data.
papers.abstract: High-throughput single-cell RNA-sequencing (scRNA-seq) technologies have revolutionized our ability to characterize cellular heterogeneity and dissect gene regulatory mechanisms. These data, however, are inherently high-dimensional and correlated, posing substantial challenges for statistical inference and feature selection. Identifying disease-related genes, while rigorously controlling false discoveries, remains a key challenge in scRNA-seq data analysis. Traditional methods often rely on parametric assumptions, which may fail to capture complex relationships and can suffer from inflated fal
papers.summary: DiffKnock introduces a diffusion-based knockoff inference framework for neural networks, designed to identify disease-related genes in scRNA-seq data while rigorously controlling false discoveries. The method generates knockoff features using diffusion models, avoiding restrictive parametric assumptions that can lead to inflated false discovery rates in traditional approaches. This enables more reliable feature selection in high-dimensional, correlated single-cell data.

papers.title: Integration of single-cell multi-omic data with graph-based topic modelling.
papers.abstract: Recent advances in single-cell biology enable the profiling of multiple molecular layers, such as the transcriptome, epigenome, and surface proteins, within a single cell. Tackling the complexity of these data from multiple perspectives allows researchers to gain the most comprehensive insights into cellular biological properties. Here, we propose a graph-based topic modelling method called bionSBM. Our method leverages well-known community-detection methods for multipartite graphs and the interpretability of topic modelling to cluster and explain high-dimensional, sparse, and noisy single-cel
papers.summary: The authors present bionSBM, a graph-based topic modelling method for integrating single-cell multi-omic data across modalities such as transcriptome, epigenome, and surface proteins. It combines community-detection algorithms for multipartite graphs with topic modelling to cluster cells and provide interpretable explanations of high-dimensional, sparse, and noisy single-cell data.

papers.title: Disagreement-informed arbitration for gene regulatory network inference: A score-level meta-classifier and a diagnostic typology of inter-method conflict.
papers.abstract: Gene regulatory network inference methods routinely disagree about individual edges, and practitioners resolve those conflicts by choosing one method or averaging them all. We ask whether the conflict can instead be arbitrated per edge. A gradient-boosted classifier is trained on the raw scores that ten inference methods-correlation-based, information-theoretic, sparse-regression and tree-ensemble, including GENIE3, GRNBoost2, CLR and ARACNe-assign to each candidate regulator-target pair, so that the weight given to each method varies from edge to edge. Across six single-cell perturbation scre
papers.summary: The authors propose a per-edge arbitration approach for gene regulatory network inference, training a gradient-boosted classifier on the raw scores from ten different inference methods to decide which method to trust for each candidate regulator-target pair. This replaces the common practice of picking one method or averaging all methods, and the paper also offers a diagnostic typology of why methods conflict. The approach is evaluated across six single-cell perturbation screens.

papers.title: Integrated single-cell and bulk transcriptomic analysis reveals an epithelial cell-derived prognostic and immunotherapeutic signature with ADAM12 as a key functional regulator in non-small cell lung cancer.
papers.abstract: This study developed a Prognostic and Immunotherapeutic Signature (PIS) for NSCLC using single-cell and bulk RNA-seq data. By integrating TCGA and GEO datasets with machine learning, we identified key epithelial cells-related genes predictive of immunotherapy response. PIS effectively stratifies patients by survival and immune activity, with low-PIS individuals showing better outcomes and higher immune infiltration. We confirmed the high expression of ADAM12 in both tissue samples and cell lines, and validated its functional roles through cellular assays. Furthermore, mouse model experiments d
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell and bulk RNA-seq data from NSCLC to build a Prognostic and Immunotherapeutic Signature (PIS) based on epithelial cell-derived genes, using machine learning to stratify patients by survival and immune activity. Low-PIS patients showed better outcomes and higher immune infiltration, and ADAM12 was validated experimentally as a key functional regulator in tissue samples, cell lines, and mouse models. The work links epithelial cell states to immunotherapy response prediction in lung cancer.

papers.title: A categorization of spatial transcriptomics methods for cell-cell communication analysis.
papers.abstract: Cell-cell communication (CCC) is involved in regulating cellular behavior in tissues. Spatial transcriptomics adds local context to gene expression, enabling more biologically grounded CCC inference than single-cell RNA-seq alone. Rapid method development has yielded diverse CCC methods, each addressing distinct biological questions through varied analytical frameworks. We review 33 recent methods and organize them into three categories: inference of communication networks at cell-type or single-cell resolution, modeling of microenvironment-driven transcriptional variability and regulatory mod
papers.summary: This review categorizes 33 recent computational methods for inferring cell-cell communication from spatial transcriptomics data into three groups: cell-type or single-cell resolution network inference, modeling of microenvironment-driven transcriptional variability, and regulatory modulation. It highlights how spatial context enables more biologically grounded communication inference than scRNA-seq alone and maps methods to the distinct biological questions they address.

papers.title: A contextual activity score (CAS) for inferring ADAR-associated transcriptional activity across RNA-seq, single-cell, and spatial transcriptomics.
papers.abstract: Adenosine-to-inosine RNA editing, catalyzed by Adenosine Deaminases Acting on RNA (ADARs), is a widespread modification involved in neural function, immune regulation, and cancer. The Alu Editing Index (AEI) is the standard metric to estimate ADAR activity but requires raw sequencing reads and is poorly suited for single-cell and spatial transcriptomic data. This study aimed to develop an alternative framework for inferring ADAR-associated transcriptional activity from gene expression data across diverse transcriptomic technologies.
papers.journal: Computer methods and programs in biomedicine
papers.summary: The authors introduce a Contextual Activity Score (CAS) that infers ADAR-associated RNA editing activity directly from gene expression data, bypassing the need for raw sequencing reads required by the standard Alu Editing Index. This makes it applicable to single-cell and spatial transcriptomics, where read-level editing quantification is impractical. The framework enables estimation of ADAR activity across diverse transcriptomic platforms.

papers.title: An integrated transcriptional and post-transcriptional regulatory circuit orchestrated by NUDT21 maintains the proliferation and survival of neuroblastoma.
papers.abstract: Neuroblastoma (NB) is the most prevalent pediatric solid tumor associated with a poor prognosis. While alternative polyadenylation (APA) is a key post-transcriptional regulatory mechanism in many cancers, its role in NB remains largely unexplored.
papers.summary: This study investigates how alternative polyadenylation (APA), a post-transcriptional regulatory mechanism, contributes to neuroblastoma, the most common pediatric solid tumor. The authors identify NUDT21 as a central orchestrator of an integrated transcriptional and post-transcriptional circuit that sustains neuroblastoma cell proliferation and survival, suggesting APA regulation as a potential therapeutic vulnerability in this cancer.

papers.title: SWINGOT: Spatially Weighted Integration of Multi-Omics with Graph Optimal Transport.
papers.abstract: Background: Spatial multi-omics technologies help study tissue organization and spatial molecular patterns, but integration remains challenging. We aimed to integrate paired spatial multi-omics data while preserving relationships among spatial spots. Methods: We developed SWINGOT (Spatially Weighted Integration of Multi-Omics with Graph Optimal Transport), a topology-aware framework combining Wasserstein-based distribution alignment and Gromov-Wasserstein-based relational regularization. A conservative residual gated fusion strategy integrates modality-specific representations while limiting s
papers.summary: SWINGOT is a new computational framework for integrating paired spatial multi-omics datasets while preserving the spatial relationships between tissue spots. It combines Wasserstein-based distribution alignment with Gromov-Wasserstein-based relational regularization, plus a residual gated fusion strategy to merge modality-specific representations without letting one modality dominate. The method addresses a key challenge in spatial multi-omics analysis: keeping spatial topology intact during cross-modality integration.

papers.title: Lineage-mixed neurodevelopmental programs in pediatric sarcomas nominate tumor-selective surface antigen pairs.
papers.abstract: Pediatric solid tumors have low mutational burden, frequent oncogenic gene fusions, and developmental origins in arrested progenitor cells. Single-cell RNA-seq (scRNA-seq) could represent an ideal tool to assess whether these convergent biological features yield shared therapeutic vulnerabilities. However, while existing tools can extract gene expression programs for pan-tumor single-cell data, interpreting them requires domain expertise across many disciplines and diseases. Here, we analyzed a pan-pediatric scRNA-seq atlas of 266 patient-and xenograft-derived samples across 22 pediatric solid
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors analyzed a pan-pediatric single-cell RNA-seq atlas of 266 samples spanning 22 pediatric solid tumor types and found that these tumors express lineage-mixed neurodevelopmental gene programs, reflecting their origins in arrested progenitor cells. From these programs they identified tumor-selective pairs of surface antigens that could serve as targets for combinatorial therapy, offering a strategy to improve tumor specificity while sparing normal tissue.

papers.title: HOMED enables hierarchical and multimodal optimization of DNA methylation deconvolution across tissues.
papers.abstract: Cellular heterogeneity is a major confounder in bulk DNA methylation data used in epigenome-wide association studies. Existing reference-based DNAm deconvolution methods often overlook hierarchical relationships among related cell types and may generalize poorly across datasets due to limited variability in reference profiles. We developed HOMED (Hierarchically Optimized Methylation Deconvolution), a framework that integrates cell-type hierarchy, single-cell RNA sequencing-guided deconvolution, and paired bulk RNA-seq/DNAm data for CpG signature optimization. Across multiple simulated and real
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: HOMED is a new computational framework for DNA methylation deconvolution that accounts for hierarchical relationships among related cell types, uses single-cell RNA-seq to guide signature selection, and leverages paired bulk RNA-seq/DNAm data to optimize CpG signatures. This improves estimation of cell-type proportions in bulk methylation data across tissues, addressing a key confounder in epigenome-wide association studies.

papers.title: Categorization and analysis of 16 computational methods for estimating cell potency from single-cell RNA-seq data.
papers.abstract: Inferring hidden cellular dynamics from static single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data remains a critical challenge. Beyond pseudotime trajectories and RNA velocities, cell potency provides another perspective by estimating cellular differentiation potential from gene expression levels. We review 16 computational methods that define cell potency under different, sometimes contrasting, assumptions. On the basis of how they summarize gene expression into a potency measure, we categorize them into average-based, entropy-based, and knowledge-based methods. Using a unified set of mathematical n
papers.summary: This review categorizes 16 computational methods for estimating cell potency (differentiation potential) from static single-cell RNA-seq data into average-based, entropy-based, and knowledge-based approaches. The authors analyze these methods under a unified mathematical framework, highlighting their differing and sometimes contrasting assumptions. The work provides guidance for choosing appropriate potency estimation tools and clarifies the conceptual foundations of this emerging analytical perspective.

papers.title: ETS1 as a Candidate Biomarker for Sepsis‑Associated Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome: Multi‑Omics Analysis and Clinical Validation.
papers.abstract: This multi‑omics study aimed to screen candidate molecules associated with the transition from sepsis to sepsis‑associated ARDS, and provide preliminary biological evidence for risk‑stratification research.
papers.summary: This study integrates multi-omics data with clinical validation to identify ETS1 as a candidate biomarker associated with the progression from sepsis to sepsis-associated acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS). The findings provide preliminary biological evidence supporting ETS1 as a potential tool for risk stratification in sepsis patients.

papers.title: Integration of bulk and single-cell transcriptomics via the Scissor algorithm reveals APOE-dependent cholesterol metabolic reprogramming in macrophages associated with osimertinib resistance in non-small cell lung cancer.
papers.abstract: The tumor microenvironment contributes to acquired resistance against osimertinib in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), yet the key cell subpopulations and the underlying metabolic mechanisms remain incompletely elucidated.
papers.summary: This study applies the Scissor algorithm to integrate bulk and single-cell transcriptomic data, identifying macrophage subpopulations linked to osimertinib resistance in NSCLC. The authors report that these resistance-associated macrophages show APOE-dependent cholesterol metabolic reprogramming, nominating a metabolic axis in the tumor microenvironment as a potential contributor to acquired resistance.

papers.title: A ten-gene tyrosine-metabolism signature defines prognosis and reveals metabo-immune suppression in low-grade astrocytoma.
papers.abstract: Emerging evidence implicates dysregulated tyrosine metabolism in glioma malignancy; however, its cell-type specificity and clinical relevance in low-grade astrocytoma (LGA) remain undefined.
papers.summary: This study identifies a ten-gene signature related to tyrosine metabolism that is associated with prognosis in low-grade astrocytoma. The signature appears to reflect a state of metabolic and immune suppression, suggesting a link between tyrosine metabolism and immune evasion in these tumors.

papers.title: Spatial and single-cell transcriptomics identify a CD276-rich vascular matrix-associated CAF state linked to adverse outcomes under targeted therapy-immunotherapy combinations in clear cell renal cell carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Targeted therapy-immunotherapy combinations have improved treatment outcomes in advanced clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC), but primary non-response and post-treatment residual progression remain common. Cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) exhibit marked heterogeneity and are closely associated with tumor treatment tolerance; however, specific stromal states associated with treatment non-response, post-treatment residual disease, and immune exclusion remain insufficiently characterized.
papers.summary: Using spatial and single-cell transcriptomics on clear cell renal cell carcinoma samples, the authors identify a distinct cancer-associated fibroblast state marked by high CD276 expression that is embedded in the vascular matrix. This CAF state is associated with immune exclusion and poor outcomes in patients receiving targeted therapy–immunotherapy combinations.

papers.title: Integrated multi-omics analysis supports a causal association of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease with benign prostatic hyperplasia and interactions between VCAN-high fibroblasts and macrophages in hyperplastic prostate tissue.
papers.abstract: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) are common among middle-aged and older men and can coexist clinically. However, the direction of causality and the underlying biological links between them remain unclear.
papers.summary: This study uses integrated multi-omics and Mendelian randomization to test whether COPD causally influences benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH), finding evidence for a causal association. It further identifies an interaction between VCAN-high fibroblasts and macrophages in hyperplastic prostate tissue as a potential biological link. The work suggests shared molecular mechanisms between the two age-related conditions.

papers.title: Identification and characterization of ion channel-related signatures in ulcerative colitis: an integrated multi-omics and machine learning analysis.
papers.abstract: Ulcerative colitis (UC) is a chronic, multifactorial inflammatory bowel disease characterized by persistent mucosal inflammation and immune dysregulation. Human ion channel genes (HICGs) are involved in maintaining cellular homeostasis and regulating immune function, but their expression patterns and diagnostic value in UC have not been systematically investigated. This study aimed to identify UC-associated HICGs and evaluate their potential as diagnostic biomarkers using an integrative multi-omics approach.
papers.summary: This study integrates multi-omics data with machine learning to identify ion channel genes whose expression patterns distinguish ulcerative colitis from healthy tissue. The authors characterize these genes as candidate diagnostic biomarkers, linking ion channel dysregulation to the immune dysfunction seen in UC. The work is exploratory and biomarker-focused, with findings that would need independent validation before clinical use.

papers.title: Integrated bulk, single-nucleus, spatial transcriptomic, and proteomic analyses identify Crot-associated proximal-tubule peroxisomal dysregulation in murine renal ischemia-reperfusion injury.
papers.abstract: Renal ischemia-reperfusion injury (IRI) underlies acute kidney injury after transplantation, shock, and major surgery. Proximal-tubule metabolic dysfunction shapes injury and repair. Peroxisomes shorten fatty acids and export products, but their cross-omic behavior in acute renal IRI remains unclear.
papers.summary: This study integrates bulk, single-nucleus, spatial transcriptomic, and proteomic data to characterize proximal-tubule injury in a mouse model of renal ischemia-reperfusion injury. The authors identify dysregulation of peroxisomal pathways associated with the Crot gene, linking metabolic dysfunction in proximal tubules to acute kidney injury. The work provides a multi-omic resource for understanding injury and repair mechanisms in renal IRI.

papers.title: A deep-learning microglial response score integrates single-cell and spatial transcriptomics for Alzheimer's disease stratification.
papers.abstract: Microglia exhibit diverse responses in Alzheimer's disease (AD), yet linking these responses to tissue pathology and disease heterogeneity remains challenging. We aimed to develop a deep-learning microglial response score (DL-MRS) integrating single-cell, spatial and bulk transcriptomics to characterize AD-associated transcriptional patterns.
papers.summary: The authors introduce a deep-learning microglial response score (DL-MRS) that combines single-cell, spatial, and bulk transcriptomic data to characterize microglial transcriptional states in Alzheimer's disease. This integrated score is proposed as a tool for stratifying AD patients by microglial response patterns, potentially linking cellular states to tissue pathology and disease heterogeneity.

papers.title: The predictive dermatome: a technical framework for spatial AI mapping of molecular skin aging.
papers.abstract: Skin aging is spatially heterogeneous. Chronological age and most systemic aging clocks provide useful population-level estimates, but they do not explain why adjacent or anatomically distinct skin regions may show different rates of dermal thinning, matrix remodeling, pigmentation change, vascular fragility, inflammation, or treatment response. We define the Predictive Dermatome as a computationally derived, anatomically localized skin region characterized by a shared or probabilistically related biological aging state and trajectory inferred from integrated molecular, structural, imaging, cl
papers.summary: The paper proposes the 'Predictive Dermatome' framework, which uses spatial AI to integrate molecular, structural, and imaging data to define anatomically localized skin regions with shared biological aging trajectories. This addresses the limitation of systemic aging clocks that cannot explain spatial heterogeneity in skin aging, such as differing rates of dermal thinning or pigmentation changes across adjacent regions.

papers.title: A metabolic state in the cancer-associated fibroblast differentiation continuum of colorectal cancer.
papers.abstract: The metabolic heterogeneity of cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) in the colorectal cancer (CRC) microenvironment remains poorly understood.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
papers.summary: This study investigates metabolic heterogeneity among cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) in colorectal cancer, identifying a distinct metabolic state within the CAF differentiation continuum. The findings suggest that CAF metabolic states may be linked to their functional roles in the tumor microenvironment, though the abstract provides limited detail on specific metabolic pathways or clinical implications.

papers.title: Single-cell multi-omics reveals cellular atlases and cell-cell interaction networks in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD).
papers.abstract: To summarize recent advances in single-cell multi-omics technologies in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), with a focus on cellular atlases, cellular heterogeneity, and intercellular communication networks in hepatic and extrahepatic tissues.
papers.summary: This review summarizes how single-cell multi-omics technologies are being applied to MASLD, focusing on the construction of cellular atlases, characterization of cellular heterogeneity, and mapping of intercellular communication networks across hepatic and extrahepatic tissues. It consolidates recent advances to illustrate how these approaches reveal disease-relevant cell states and interaction circuits that bulk profiling cannot resolve.

papers.title: Clinical and single-cell integration identifies a TCF21-associated stromal death-inflammation signature in endometriosis.
papers.abstract: Stromal heterogeneity, regulated-cell-death-associated stress, and chronic inflammation contribute to endometriosis, but their relationships within specific stromal populations remain incompletely understood. This study integrated clinical characterization with single-cell and spatial transcriptomics to investigate a TCF21-associated stromal death-inflammation signature.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
papers.summary: This study integrates clinical data with single-cell and spatial transcriptomics to characterize stromal heterogeneity in endometriosis, identifying a TCF21-associated stromal population linked to regulated cell death and chronic inflammation. The work proposes a 'death-inflammation signature' that may help explain how specific stromal subsets contribute to disease pathology.

papers.title: Multi-omics characterization of fibroblast subpopulations involved in osteogenic differentiation in periodontitis.
papers.abstract: Fibroblasts are the predominant stromal cells in periodontal tissues and are involved in inflammation and repair. However, their heterogeneity and molecular mechanisms remain poorly defined. Our study is to identify fibroblast subpopulations driving osteogenesis in periodontitis and their molecular markers.
papers.summary: This study uses multi-omics profiling to identify distinct fibroblast subpopulations in periodontal tissue and characterize those that drive osteogenic differentiation during periodontitis. The authors propose molecular markers for these osteogenic fibroblast subsets, offering a framework for understanding fibroblast heterogeneity in inflammation and repair.

papers.title: Multi-source analysis identifies an NPC2-associated macrophage transcriptional program in ulcerative colitis.
papers.abstract: Ulcerative colitis (UC) involves extensive remodeling of intestinal macrophage states, but the molecular programs linking inflammation, lysosomal function, and lipid handling remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to identify macrophage-associated molecules and cellular states linked to UC.
papers.summary: This study integrates multiple transcriptomic datasets to identify a macrophage transcriptional program associated with NPC2, a lysosomal lipid-binding protein, in ulcerative colitis. The authors propose that this NPC2-associated program links inflammation with lysosomal function and lipid handling in intestinal macrophages, highlighting a candidate molecular axis for further investigation in UC.
